div.head: II Cn 30.1
div.ab: Gyf se hlaford þonne secge, þæt him naðor ne að ne ordal ne burste, syððan þæt gemot wæs on Winceastre, nime se hlaford him twegen getrywe men to innon þam hundrede, ⁊ swerian, þæt him næfre að ne burste ne ordal, [ne he] þeofgyld ne gulde, butan he þone gerefan hæbbe, þe ðæs wyrðe sig, þe þæt don mæge.

Gyf se hlaford ðonne secge, þæt him naðor ne burste ne að ne ordal, syþðan þæt gemot wæs on Winceastre, níme se hlaford him twegen getrywe men to innan ðam hundrede, and swerian, þæt him nǽfre að ne burste ne ordal, ne ðeófgyld ne gulde, buton hé ðone gerefan hæbbe, [þe þæs wurþe si], ðe þæt don mæge.

Gif se hlaford þonne secge, þæt him naðor ne að ne ordal ne burste, syððan þæt gemot wæs on Winceastre, nime se hlaford him twegen getrywe men to innan þam hundrede, ⁊ swerian, þæt him næfre að ne burste ne ordal, ne he þeofgyld ne gulde, buton he þonne gereafan hæbbe, þe þæs wyrðe sy, þe þæt don mage.

Si dominus eius dicat tunc, quod ei neutrum uel iuramentum uel ordalium fregerit, postquam concilium fuit apud Wincestram, assumat idem dominus secum duos credibiles homines in ipso hundreto et iuret, quod illi nunquam iuramentum uel ordalium fregit, nec furigildum reddidit, nisi talem prepositum habeat, qui eo dignus sit, qui hoc facere possit.

Quodsi dominus eius dixerit, quia nunquam illi fregerit iuramentum (sacramentum) nec iudicium, nec prętium latrocinii persoluit, tunc ille dominus accipiat secum duos fideles et hoc ita esse sacramento affirmet, nisi talem prępositum habeat, qui dignus sit hoc idem pro eo facere.

Quodsi dominus illius asserat, quod ille numquam in iuramento uel de iudicio cecidisset, postquam conuentus factus est apud Wincestriam, assumat ipse dominus sibi duos fideles de ipso centenario, qui secum iurent, quod illi numquam defecerat iuramentum uel Dei iudicium, nec unquam furis tributum soluerat, nisi prepositum habeat qui hoc facere pro illo dignus sit.

Gyf se hlaford ðonne secge þæt him naðor ne burste ne að ne ordal syþðan þæt gemot wæs on Winceastre, níme se hlaford him twegen getrywe men to innan ðam hundrede, and swerian þæt him nǽfre að ne burste ne ordal ne ðeófgyld ne gulde—buton hé ðone gerefan hæbbe þe þæs wurþe si ðe þæt don mæge.

Gyf se hlaford þonne secge þæt him naðor ne að ne ordal ne burste syððan þæt gemot wæs on Winceastre, nime se hlaford him twegen getrywe men to innon þam hundrede, and swerian þæt him næfre að ne burste ne ordal, ne he þeofgyld ne gulde, butan he þone gerefan hæbbe, þe ðæs wyrðe sig, þe þæt don mæge.

Wenn der Herr [desselben] freilich behauptet, dass jenem, seitdem der Reichstag zu Winchester war, weder Eid noch Ordal fehlgeschlagen sei, so wähle sich der Herr zwei vertrauenswürdige Männer hinzu innerhalb dieser [einen] Hundertschaft, und [diese drei] sollen schwören, ‘dass jenem nie weder Eid fehlschlug noch Ordal, noch er Diebesbusse bezahlen musste’ — es sei denn, der [Herr] habe einen solchen Amtmann, der dazu berechtigt ist, dass er dies thun dürfe [statt des Gutsherrn].

But if his lord asserts that neither oath nor ordeal has failed him since the assembly at Winchester, let the lord take two trustworthy men within that [one] hundred, and [these three] are to swear ‘that neither oath nor ordeal ever failed him, nor did he have to pay theft-compensation’ — unless [the lord] has a reeve who is entitled to do this [in place of the lord].

If, however, his lord asserts that he has failed neither in oath nor in ordeal since the assembly was held at Winchester, he (the lord) shall choose two trustworthy men within the hundred—unless he have a reeve who is qualified to discharge this duty—and they shall swear that he has never failed in oath or in ordeal or been convicted of stealing.

If the lord then says that he has failed neither at oath nor at ordeal since the assembly was held at Winchester, the lord is to take with him two trustworthy men from within the hundred and swear that he failed neither at oath nor at ordeal, nor did he pay any compensation for theft, unless the lord have a reeve who is entitled to do this on his behalf.

Yet if his lord declares that he has failed neither oath nor ordeal since the court was held at Winchester, then the lord shall appoint two men from within the hundred to swear that he has never failed an oath or ordeal, nor has he been convicted of theft, unless he has a reeve entitled to do this.

note.label: repeats
note.quote: This chapter repeats I Ethelred, 1.2 (cf. also III Ethelred, 4), except that Winchester is substituted for Bromdun

note.label: earlier version
note.quote: An earlier version of this clause appears in 1 Æthelred 1.2, with Bromdun cited as the relevant assembly rather than Winchester.

div.note: G's ‘[ne he]’ is on an erasure in the 16th century. Liebermann compares I Atr 1.2.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 331, October 2026 (MS Cons)
ne he: added in a sixteenth-century hand over an erasure in G

Winchester: An earlier version of this clause appears in 1 Æthelred 1.2, with Bromdun cited as the relevant assembly rather than Winchester. The meeting referred to here is presumably the one at which 1 Cnut and 2 Cnut were issued. See 1 Cnut Pr.

Kein früheres, sondern das gegenwärtige Gesetz ist gemeint; s. o. Einl. 13
No earlier law is meant, but the present one; see above Introduction 13

‘Thegn’ der Quelle vermeidet Cn auch u. 30, 7³: entweder fordert er vielleicht nur Charakter, nicht Stand vom Eideshelfer (doch 31, 1a lässt er letzteren ungeändert stehen); oder wahrscheinlicher nimmt er Thegn (s. d. Gl 8) im Sinne ‘vollfrei’

Cn avoids the source's ‘thegn’ also below 30, 7³: either he perhaps requires only character, not rank, of the oath-helper (yet in 31, 1a he leaves the latter unchanged); or, more probably, he takes thegn (see that word in Gl 8) in the sense ‘fully free’
i.e. (apparently) ‘from the present time onwards.’ The words are taken from I Atr. 1, 2, with the substitution of Winchester for Bromdun.

note.label: si
note.seg: þe þ. w. si. Added in the margin in 16th cent. in B.

note.label: behalf
note.seg: This chapter repeats I Ethelred, 1.2 (cf. also III Ethelred, 4), except that Winchester is substituted for Bromdun, and that Ethelred required the oath-helpers to be thegns. The following chapters also are mainly from I Ethelred, but paragraphs 30.30 and 30.5 are new, and 30.4 substitutes mutilation for the death-penalty.
